REGULAR MEETING AGENDA CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY THURSDAY - JANUARY 11, 2018 - CITY HALL - 07:00 P.M. City Council Chamber AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted. PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter. 1. Call to Order 2. Invocation The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution. Invocation 3. Pledge of Allegiance Pledge of Allegiance Invocation 4. Roll Call 5. Presentations Presentations 6. Public Comments and Suggestions 7. Consent Calendar Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately. 7A. Approval of Minutes Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of December 14, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). Agenda Report 7B. Approval of Register of Demands Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 11, 2018 (COUNCIL). Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency dated January 11, 2018 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY). Agenda Report 7C. Approval of Treasurer's Reports Approval of the City Council Treasurer's report for the period ending November 30, 2017 (COUNCIL). Approval of the Successor Agency Treasurer's report for the period ending November 30, 2017 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY). Agenda Report 7D. Adoption of Ordinance Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of December 14, 2017: Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance 1019, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, MOVING THE DATE OF THE CITY'S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION FROM THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL IN ODD-NUMBERED YEARS TO THE FIRST TUESDAY AFTER THE FIRST MONDAY IN MARCH OF EVEN-NUMBERED YEARS COMMENCING NO EARLIER THAN MARCH 3, 2020 (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 7E. Award of a contract for Loma Park Playground improvements, Project No. 18101, Bid No. 1330-17 (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 8. Public Hearings 8A. Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS PROHIBITING PARKING ON A PORTION OF DENNI STREET NORTH OF LA PALMA AVENUE (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 9. New and Old Business 9A. Review and consideration of providing free Cerritos Library cards for students attending Bellflower Unified School District schools (COUNCIL). Agenda Report Supplemental Correspondence Notice 9B. Review and discussion of an informational report on the City's tree trimming progress (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 9C. Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING THE SUBMISSION OF AN ATTESTATION OF THE VERACITY OF THE POWER SOURCE DISCLOSURE ANNUAL REPORT TO THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 9D. Review and consideration of a recommendation of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission to place a first responders memorial in the Cerritos Civic Center near the Cerritos Sheriff's Station and to provide funding from the Art in Public Places Trust Fund.Â  The proposed project site is generally located on the northwest corner of Bloomfield Avenue and 183rd Street, west of Cerritos City Hall (APN 7025-028-905) (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 10. Legislative Items 10A. Report on pending legislation 10B. Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature. 11. City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item. 12. Closed Session 13. Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JANUARY 11, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by Pastor Dustin T. Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by City of Cerritos Recreation Services Division,
  Youth Basketball League Team Rookie III – The Dunk Stars.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations

  Proclamation presented to:
  Lynda Johnson (Recognition of service for the ABC Unified School District).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  C.W. Van der Linden, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding crime in the City, how
  to address it and recommended recognizing those who report crimes.

  Luis Angel Soto, Cerritos resident, spoke on term limits and recommended changes
  for the City Attorney and City Manager positions.

  Christopher Craig, State Assembly Member Christina Garcia's Office, encouraged
  residents of the 58th District to participate in the Community Bill idea contest, "There
  Ought to be a Law," and recognizing the community with the “Pride 58” Monthly
  Spotlight program.

  Daisy Velasco, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding trimming trees to improve
  lighting and the need for an Alzheimer's facility in Cerritos.

  Joseph DiDonato, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding a code enforcement
  violation, stated the problem is related to overgrown tree roots and that he is
  waiting on a removal decision with the remaining tree.

  Sam Desai, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding crime, requested more support
  for Neighborhood Watch programs and review of small business start-up
  requirements.
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Mel Cortez, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding crime in the City, and suggested
  the City put aside 1% of the valuation of projects into a safety fund to combat
  crime.

  Murali Vasudeuan, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding crime in the City and the
  Juliet project.

  Kathleen Joslin, Cerritos resident, spoke in opposition to the Juliet project.

  Charles Joslin, Cerritos resident, expressed his opposition to the Juliet project.

  Rod and Judi Dixon, Cerritos residents, spoke in opposition to the Juliet project.

  Jay Gray, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding crime, LED lighting, keeping
  Cerritos safe, and the Juliet project.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  December 14, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of December 14, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Register of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 11,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated January 11, 2018 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  1/11/2018  $8,098,025.86  (COUNCIL)
  2. Successor Agency  1/11/2018  $1,891.92  (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar

7B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council Treasurer’s report for the period ending November
  30, 2017 (COUNCIL).

  Approval of the Successor Agency Treasurer’s report for the period ending
  November 30, 2017 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Treasurer's reports for  the  period  ending  November  30,  2017.
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Adoption of Ordinance

  Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of December 14, 2017:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance 1019, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS RESIDENT, CALIFORNIA, MOVING THE
  DATE OF THE CITY’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION FROM THE SECOND
  TUESDAY OF APRIL IN ODD-NUMBERED YEARS TO THE FIRST TUESDAY AFTER
  THE FIRST MONDAY IN MARCH OF EVEN-NUMBERED YEARS COMMENCING NO
  EARLIER THAN MARCH 3, 2020 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to waive full
  reading and adopt:

  Ordinance 1019, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS RESIDENT, CALIFORNIA, MOVING THE DATE OF THE CITY’S
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION FROM THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL
  IN ODD-NUMBERED YEARS TO THE FIRST TUESDAY AFTER THE FIRST
  MONDAY IN MARCH OF EVEN-NUMBERED YEARS COMMENCING NO
  EARLIER THAN MARCH 3, 2020 (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar

7D.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of a contract for Loma Park Playground improvements, Project No. 18101,
  Bid No. 1330-17 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Award a contract in the amount of $121,503 for Loma Park Playground
  improvements, Project No. 18101, Bid No. 1330-17 to RE Schultz and reject
  the other bid; and
  2.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS PROHIBITING PARKING ON A
  PORTION OF DENNI STREET NORTH OF LA PALMA AVENUE (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Joan Pylman, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding problems in the park, standing
  water, overgrown trees, street maintenance and stated she is neutral to the
  parking restrictions.

  Sheila Gibbons, Cerritos resident, spoke regarding safety, and expressed her
  support of the resolution.

  Sandra Hojo, Cerritos resident, expressed her support of the parking restriction,
  and suggested it include an amendment for no parking at any time.

  Patrick Graham, La Palma resident, spoke in opposition to parking restrictions as
  proposed, increase lighting by trimming trees, and the need for increased law
  enforcement.
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 8
8.  Public Hearings (continued)
8A.  (continued)
  Roland Colmo, Cerritos resident, expressed his support for the resolution and
  suggested implementing a trial no parking zone to determine how it would affect
  crime.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2018-01, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS PROHIBITING PARKING ON A
  PORTION OF DENNI STREET NORTH OF LA PALMA AVENUE (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of providing free Cerritos Library cards for students
  attending Bellflower Unified School District schools (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Nahim Banks, Bellflower High School student, spoke in support of the item.

  Martha Quintanilla, Bellflower High School student, spoke in support of the item.

  Omar Subeh, Cerritos College student, spoke in support of the item.

  C.W. Van der Linden, Cerritos resident, spoke in opposition to the item.

  Sam Desai, Cerritos resident, spoke in opposition to the item.

  Nick Wagner, Bellflower, spoke in support of the item.

  Daisy Velasco, Cerritos resident, spoke in opposition to the item.

  Gerald Greenidge, Cerritos resident, spoke in support of the item.

  Bryan Thornhill, Cerritos resident, stated he is neutral on the matter.

  Dr. Olga Rios, ABCUSD Board Member, Lakewood, spoke in support of the item
  and read letters of support from ABCUSD colleagues.

  Jay Gray, Cerritos resident, spoke in opposition to the item.

  Murali Vasudevan, Cerritos resident, spoke in opposition to the item.
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A. (continued)

  Luis Angel Soto, Cerritos resident, spoke in support of the item.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum, Cerritos resident, spoke in support of the item.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to receive and
  file the report with no revisions to the current Cerritos Library free library card
  eligibility policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Hu
  NOES:  Yokoyama, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and discussion of an informational report on the City’s tree trimming
  progress (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent.  A PowerPoint
  presentation displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Murali Vasudevan, Cerritos resident, inquired as to why only pine trees are
  addressed and asked for public hearing on the item.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize the
  City Manager or his designee to execute a change order with Great Scott Tree
  Service in the amount of $33,500 to complete a Pine Tree Inventory in the City
  of Cerritos.

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING THE SUBMISSION
  OF AN ATTESTATION OF THE VERACITY OF THE POWER SOURCE DISCLOSURE
  ANNUAL REPORT TO THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)
9C.  (continued)

  A staff report was given by Ramzi Raufdeen, Electric Utility Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2018-02, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING THE SUBMISSION OF
  AN ATTESTATION OF THE VERACITY OF THE POWER SOURCE
  DISCLOSURE  ANNUAL  REPORT  TO  THE  CALIFORNIA  ENERGY
  COMMISSION (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of a recommendation of the Fine Arts and Historical
  Commission to place a first responders memorial in the Cerritos Civic Center
  near the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station and to provide funding from the Art in Public
  Places Trust Fund. The proposed project site is generally located on the
  northwest corner of Bloomfield Avenue and 183rd Street, west of Cerritos City
  Hall (APN 7025-028-905) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathleen Jung Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Approve the concept of a first responders memorial to be installed in the
  area near the north entrance of the Cerritos Sheriff's Station;
  2. Direct the Fine Arts and Historical Commission to continue to develop a final
  concept for the City Council review and approval; and
  3. Approve and appropriate an amount of $250,000 from the Art In Public
  Places Trust Fund for the development and construction of a first responders
  memorial.
  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  Hu
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  January 11, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 8 of 8

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Solanki, and Yokoyama,
  Mayor Pro Tem Pulido, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 12:03 a.m. on January 12, 2018.

  /s/Vida Barone  ___________
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/Grace Hu  _______ __
Grace Hu, Mayor/Chair

APPROVED: January 22, 2018
